blocks.body: Divorce is the one transition in this list where professional counsel is close to mandatory: state property law decides what is marital, and agreements are hard to reopen. If a full-service lawyer is out of reach, look for legal aid or ask whether a lawyer will help with only part of the case. Build a complete list of accounts, debts and policies first; it is also the start of your own net-worth snapshot. A decree does not bind your lenders: until a joint debt is paid off, refinanced without your name or released by the lender, the lender can generally still collect from you.
blocks.plain: Divorce is the one event on this list where a lawyer is close to a must: your state's property law decides what counts as shared, and a signed agreement is hard to undo. If you can't pay a lawyer for the whole case, look for legal aid or ask whether a lawyer will help with just part of it. First, list every account, debt and insurance policy. That list is also the start of your own net-worth snapshot. The divorce papers don't bind your lenders: until a shared debt is paid off, refinanced without your name, or the lender lets you off it, the lender can usually still make you pay.
props: Professional counsel is close to mandatory for divorce
State property law decides what is marital
If a full-service lawyer is unaffordable, look for legal aid or ask about a lawyer for only part of the case
Build a complete inventory of accounts, debts, policies first
list every account, debt and insurance policy
The inventory starts your own net-worth snapshot
A decree does not bind lenders; a creditor can generally collect on a joint debt until it is paid off, refinanced without your name, or you are released
blocks.notes: Lean: only the two HIGH fixes. The legal-aid / part-of-the-case sentence (ADV-17) and the joint-debt sentence (ADV-18) are taken verbatim from the final proposal (its P4 and P8). Left out as not HIGH: the safety/financial-control sentence (ADV-19, MED; with it CL527 and NEW-le-divorce-2 drop out) and the Social Security 10-year sentence (CFP-21, MED). No sentence of the current text was found wrong, so no MED correction is kept. Props renumbered P1-P7 (current P4/P5 become P5/P6). Neither added sentence carries a number.

blocks.body: An employer plan can only pay a former spouse under a qualified domestic relations order (QDRO); distributions to the alternate payee under a QDRO are exempt from the 10% additional tax, but the exemption does not apply to withdrawals from an IRA, so it is lost if the money is rolled into one first. IRAs are divided by a transfer incident to divorce, which is not a taxable distribution. Cashing out instead of using these routes can turn a split into a tax bill. Compare shares after tax: pre-tax retirement money is taxed when withdrawn, qualified Roth withdrawals are not, and stock you receive keeps your spouse's old tax basis, so a dollar in each is not worth the same.
blocks.plain: A job-based plan can only pay a former spouse under a court order called a qualified domestic relations order (QDRO). Money paid to the former spouse under a QDRO skips the extra 10% tax, but that break does not apply to withdrawals from an IRA, so it is lost if the money is moved into an IRA first. An IRA is split by a transfer made as part of the divorce, which isn't taxed as a withdrawal. Cashing out instead of using these routes can turn the split into a tax bill. Compare what each share is worth after tax: pre-tax retirement money is taxed when you take it out, qualified Roth withdrawals are not, and stock you receive keeps your spouse's old tax cost, so a dollar of each is not worth the same.
props: Employer plans pay a former spouse only under a QDRO
QDRO distributions to the alternate payee are exempt from the 10% additional tax
The exemption does not apply to IRA withdrawals, so rolling the money into an IRA first loses it
IRAs are divided by transfer incident to divorce, not taxable
transfer made as part of the divorce
Cashing out instead can create a tax bill
Compare shares after tax: pre-tax money is taxed on withdrawal, qualified Roth withdrawals are not, received stock keeps the old basis
blocks.notes: Lean: CFP-20 (HIGH) only, both halves: the IRA-rollover limit on the 10% exemption and the after-tax comparison sentence, verbatim from the final proposal. The final's merged clause also carried ADV-20's (MED) 'but they are generally still taxable income' / 'but it is usually still taxed as income'; that clause was cut and the IRA clause joined to the exemption clause with 'but' (plain: 'but that break', in place of the final's new sentence 'That break'). The current text is incomplete there, not stated wrong, so it is not kept as a correction. NEW-le-divorce-5 is still cited (it backs the IRA clause) and is copied unchanged, so its claim row also states the taxable-income point the lean text no longer makes. Number set unchanged: 10% in both variants.

blocks.body: Many states automatically revoke an ex-spouse as beneficiary of some non-probate assets, but for employer plans governed by ERISA the Supreme Court held that the plan documents control (Egelhoff v. Egelhoff, 2001). Do not rely on state law: file new forms on every account and policy.
blocks.plain: Many states automatically remove an ex-spouse as beneficiary on some accounts. But for job-based plans covered by ERISA, the Supreme Court ruled that the plan's own papers win (Egelhoff v. Egelhoff, 2001). Don't count on state law: file new beneficiary forms on every account and policy.
props: Many states auto-revoke an ex-spouse on some non-probate assets
For ERISA plans, plan documents control (Egelhoff, 2001)
File new forms everywhere rather than relying on state law
blocks.notes: Unchanged: no HIGH finding. ADV-21 and CFP-22 (MED, sequencing: possible restraint on beneficiary changes while the case is pending, decree-required life insurance) are left to the full proposal; their reasons say the sequencing point stands but do not call the current text factually wrong, so they were not kept as a correction. blocks.body: Marital status on December 31 sets filing status for the year. Losing coverage under a spouse's plan is a COBRA qualifying event (up to 36 months for a former spouse) and a Marketplace special enrollment trigger. For a divorce or legal separation the law puts the notice on you or your former spouse: tell the plan administrator within 60 days of the event, or the COBRA right can be lost.
blocks.plain: Whether you're married on December 31 sets your filing status for the year. Losing coverage under a spouse's plan lets you use COBRA (up to 36 months for a former spouse) and opens a Marketplace special enrollment window. For a divorce or legal separation, the law puts the notice on you or your former spouse: tell the plan administrator within 60 days of the event, or you can lose the COBRA right.
props: Marital status on Dec 31 sets filing status
Losing spouse-plan coverage is a COBRA qualifying event, up to 36 months for a former spouse
It is also a Marketplace special enrollment trigger
After divorce or legal separation, the employee or former spouse must notify the plan within 60 days or the COBRA right can be lost
blocks.notes: Unchanged: its two HIGH findings (ADV-22, CFP-19, the COBRA 60-day notice) were already addressed in the current text (CL531, 2026-11-06). ADV-23 and CFP-23 (MED: head of household while still married, Form 8332, Medicaid) are left to the full proposal; CFP-23 calls the December 31 sentence an overgeneralization but the reason does not say it is wrong, so it was not kept as a correction.

blocks.body: A household that had two incomes now has one, which usually means a larger emergency fund target and a re-run of the diagnostic with your new answers.
blocks.plain: A home that ran on two incomes now runs on one. That usually means a bigger emergency fund target, and taking the diagnostic again with your new answers.
props: Usually means a larger emergency-fund target

new_claims.claim: People who cannot afford a full-service lawyer can look to legal aid (Congress established the Legal Services Corporation to fund legal assistance in noncriminal matters for people financially unable to afford it); limited-scope help, where a lawyer handles only part of the case, exists in at least some states

new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: 42 U.S.C. §2996b(a) (LSC established 'for the purpose of providing financial support for legal assistance in noncriminal proceedings or matters to persons financially unable to afford legal assistance'); California Courts self-help page ('A lawyer can handle some parts of your case while you handle others. This is called limited-scope representation.'). Limited-scope rules are set state by state; only California's page was read. Tier B for that reason. Added 2026-11-16 from the §4.4 persona pass (ADV-17). Checker 2026-11-16: content now says 'ask whether a lawyer will help with only part of the case' rather than stating limited-scope help is available everywhere.

new_claims.claim: A divorce decree that assigns a joint debt to one spouse does not bind the creditor; the creditor can still collect from anyone named as a borrower unless that person was released by the creditor or the loan was refinanced to remove them
new_claims.source: CFPB, 'Can a debt collector contact me about a debt after a divorce?'
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: CFPB Ask CFPB 1413 ('A divorce decree or property settlement may allocate debts to a specific spouse, but it doesn't change the fact that a creditor can still collect from anyone whose name appears as a borrower'; 'you are generally responsible for a debt unless you were contractually released by the creditor or your former spouse refinanced the loan and removed your name'). The CFPB adds 'state laws vary'. Added 2026-11-16 from the §4.4 persona pass (ADV-18, HIGH). Checker 2026-11-16: content now says 'refinanced without your name' and 'generally', matching the CFPB wording.

new_claims.claim: QDRO distributions to a spouse or former spouse alternate payee are generally taxable to the alternate payee; the QDRO exception to the 10% additional tax does not apply to distributions from an IRA, so it is lost once the money is rolled into one
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: IRC §402(e)(1)(A) (spouse or former spouse alternate payee 'shall be treated as the distributee'), §72(t)(2)(C) (QDRO exception), §72(t)(3)(A) ('Subparagraphs (A)(v) and (C) of paragraph (2) shall not apply to distributions from an individual retirement plan'); IRS Pub. 504 (2025) ('Benefits paid under a QDRO to the plan participant's spouse or former spouse must generally be included in the spouse's or former spouse's income'). U.S. Code 2024 edition; Pub. 504 (2025) postdates P.L. 119-21 and shows no change. Added 2026-11-16 from the §4.4 persona pass (ADV-20, CFP-20).

new_claims.claim: Assets split in a divorce differ in after-tax value: pre-tax plan money is taxable when paid out, qualified Roth IRA distributions are excluded from income, and property transferred incident to divorce keeps the transferor's adjusted basis
new_claims.note: Verified 2026-11-16 at the primary source: IRC §1041(b)(2) ('the basis of the transferee in the property shall be the adjusted basis of the transferor'), §408A(d)(1) ('Any qualified distribution from a Roth IRA shall not be includible in gross income'); IRS Pub. 504 (2025) ('Your basis in property received from your spouse ... is the same as your spouse's adjusted basis'). The comparison itself ('not worth the same') is the framework's conclusion from those rules. Designated Roth accounts in a 401(k) (§402A) were not read; the text says 'qualified Roth withdrawals' generally. Added 2026-11-16 from the §4.4 persona pass (CFP-20).

draft.title: Protect yourself and your credit first
draft.body: If you fear for your safety or your spouse controls the money, first call the national domestic violence hotline, which can connect you with local help, then open an account in your own name and pull your free credit reports. A decree does not bind your lenders: until a joint debt is paid off, refinanced without your name or released by the lender, the lender can generally still collect from you.
draft.plain: If you are afraid for your safety or your spouse controls the money, first call the national domestic violence hotline, which can connect you with help near you. Then open a bank account in your own name and get your free credit reports. The divorce papers don't bind your lenders: until a shared debt is paid off, refinanced without your name, or the lender lets you off it, the lender can usually still make you pay.
props: If safety or financial control is a concern, first call the national domestic violence hotline (which connects callers with local help), then open an account in your own name and pull free credit reports
A decree does not bind lenders; a creditor can generally collect on a joint debt until it is paid off, refinanced without your name, or you are released
draft.counsel_body_if_taken: Divorce is the one transition in this list where professional counsel is close to mandatory: state property law decides what is marital, and agreements are hard to reopen. If a full-service lawyer is out of reach, look for legal aid or ask whether a lawyer will help with only part of the case. Build a complete list of accounts, debts and policies first; it is also the start of your own net-worth snapshot. Note the date the divorce becomes final: a former spouse married 10 years or more before that date may later draw Social Security on the other's record.
